name: Muzquizopteryx
sum: Small nyctosaurid from the early Coniacian of Coahuila, Mexico — the oldest known member of its family.
holotype: UNAM IGM 8621 — El Rosario quarry, Coahuila.
material: Nearly complete articulated skeleton of an adult; a second partial wing.
exceptional: Long fossilised tendons along both forearms.
biology: Robust arms with a hatchet-shaped deltopectoral crest; a strong-flying ocean soarer.
author: Frey et al. 2006

species.name: Muzquizopteryx coahuilensis
species.author: Frey et al. 2006
species.ref: E. Frey, M.-C. Buchy, and W. Stinnesbeck, A. González González, A. di Stefano. 2006. Muzquizopteryx coahuilensis n. g., n. sp., a nyctosaurid pterosaur with soft tissue preservation from the Coniacian (Late Cretaceous) of northeast Mexico (Coahuila). Oryctos 6:19-39
